memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel. So it was named Allon Bakuth." - Gen 35:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the middle of this journey, we come across a small, tender verse. Deborah, Rebekah's old nurse, dies and is buried under an oak below Bethel — a place they named Allon Bakuth, "the oak of weeping." She was not a famous figure. She was a servant, a nurse who had cared for Jacob's mother long ago. Yet her death is recorded, her grave is marked, and the family weeps for her.

There is something moving in this. Deborah spent her life in humble, behind-the-scenes service. Most of the world would never remember her name. But God noticed her, and He saw to it that her passing was mourned and written down in His Word for all time. The faithful nurse was not forgotten.

This is a comfort for all who serve quietly, without applause. The caregivers, the helpers, the faithful workers whose names never make the headlines — God sees every one of them. In His kingdom, greatness is measured not by fame but by faithful love and service (Matt 20:26-28). Not one act of faithful service is overlooked by Him.

And the tears at the oak remind us that grief is a real part of life's journey, even for God's people. It is right to weep when we lose those we love. God does not rush us past our sorrow; He meets us in it. He treasures both the faithful servant and the tears we shed for them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I honour the quiet, faithful servants in my life?
2. Am I comforted that God sees and remembers humble service?
3. How can I let God meet me in my grief rather than rushing past it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You see and treasure even the humblest, quietest service. Comfort me in my times of weeping, and help me to honour the faithful people others overlook. Amen.
